subject: physics

sections.title: Maxwell’s Equations: Electromagnetic Waves Predicted and Observed
Production of Electromagnetic Waves
learning_objectives: Describe the electric and magnetic waves as they move out from a source, such as an AC generator.
Explain the mathematical relationship between the magnetic field strength and the electrical field strength.
Calculate the maximum strength of the magnetic field in an electromagnetic wave, given the maximum electric field strength.

sections.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
learning_objectives: List three “rules of thumb” that apply to the different frequencies along the electromagnetic spectrum.
Explain why the higher the frequency, the shorter the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave.
Draw a simplified electromagnetic spectrum, indicating the relative positions, frequencies, and spacing of the different types of radiation bands.
List and explain the different methods by which electromagnetic waves are produced across the spectrum.

sections.title: Energy in Electromagnetic Waves
learning_objectives: Explain how the energy and amplitude of an electromagnetic wave are related.
Given its power output and the heating area, calculate the intensity of a microwave oven’s electromagnetic field, as well as its peak electric and magnetic field strengths

misconception.text: The electromagnetic spectrum is arranged in order of increasing wavelength.

correction.text: It runs from radio waves to gamma rays, so the frequency increases as the wavelength decreases. The speed of every one of them in vacuum is the same.

signal.text: Our own question offers the wavelength ordering as an option.

misconception.text: The energy of an electromagnetic wave depends on how bright it is.

correction.text: The energy of a photon is set by its frequency, $E = hf$. Brightness tells you how many photons arrive, not how much energy each one carries.

signal.text: Our own question offers the brightness reading as an option.
